the performance of CS and DP scheme are comparable and that DP scheme can achieve target QoS more easily, but at the expense of over-provisioning.
both CS and DP schemes can achieve comparable bandwidth utilization and handoff dropping performance by proper manipulation.
1) both CS and DP schemes are capable of achieving similar performance, and 2) the performance difference between CS and DP schemes depends on the target QoS, and the control parameters of DP scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance comparison of CS and DP schemes for bandwidth sharing in a cellular network with multiple services.

the performance evaluation of bandwidth sharing techniques for an integrated voice/data cellular system, and the results obtained can serve as a useful guide to the network designers in choosing the most appropriate bandwidth allocation scheme.

the design and evaluation of a novel integrated voice/data cellular system that is able to support the handoff for a variety of services with different bandwidth requirements, and to provide a high quality of service (QoS) in the presence of a heavy traffic load.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both schemes have their respective strengths and weaknesses.

the CS and DP schemes are both viable techniques for bandwidth management in a multi-service wireless network, and their respective performances are comparable, but the tradeoffs are different, and thus the selection of the scheme depends on the specific application and network environment.

both DP and CS schemes are viable and can achieve comparable performance, but DP scheme may be more desirable when the target QoS can not be achieved under CS scheme, or the system has to be more flexible in handling various QoS requirement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CS based schemes should be considered as a good alternative for bandwidth allocation in multi-services mobile cellular system, when compared with DP based schemes.
, with proper tuning, the CS based scheme is a good candidate for a multi-service cellular system, and the DP based scheme can be a good candidate for voice only systems.
, for a bandwidth allocation scheme, it is important to have a good understanding of the tradeoff between the QoS requirement and the bandwidth utilization efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both CS and DP schemes should be considered for the design of multi-services cellular networks.
, in the design of the bandwidth allocation policy, the tradeoff should be carefully considered.
the design of bandwidth sharing schemes for a multi-services network should not be limited to CS and DP, and other more advanced schemes can be developed to achieve better performance.
